_comment: Shown after a heist (breach) and after a lockout. Real-world facts stay in these cards, stated plainly with a source; the game itself stays fictional.

0.title: The sleepy teller
0.real_world: Most fraud doesn't need a hack. It needs one person who wants the conversation to be over.
0.patch: Plumpurse now makes Barry read every request back out loud before paying it.
0.lesson: Barry stays wary if you rush him into something that doesn't sound like a normal end-of-shift request.

1.title: Vendor impersonation
1.real_world: You posed as a known supplier and got an invoice paid. This is business email compromise: attackers impersonate vendors or executives and ask staff to pay. The FBI ranks it among the costliest cybercrimes it tracks.
1.patch: Plumpurse now calls vendors back on the number in the registry before paying any invoice.
1.lesson: Front-desk staff check the vendor list. Use a vendor that's on it, a believable reason, and stay under the petty cash limit.

2.title: The approval that looked right
2.real_world: Both signers approved a payment to an address neither of them knew, because the story around it checked out. In February 2025, Bybit's signers approved a transaction their screen misrepresented, and about $1.5 billion in ether left the exchange. The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, also known as Lazarus.
2.patch: Plumpurse now requires approvers to match the raw recipient against the registry, not the story, and to confirm address changes by calling the vendor back.
2.lesson: The approver sees the real recipient. Your story has to explain an unknown address with something already on file.

source.label: FBI PSA: North Korea responsible for $1.5 billion Bybit hack (Feb 26, 2025)

3.title: Past the allowlist
3.real_world: An allowlist plus a timelock is a strong defense: a direct transfer was refused no matter how good your story was. You only got through by talking both executives into adding you first. Lazarus-style operations run exactly this kind of long, patient con.
3.patch: Plumpurse now needs a board member to confirm every allowlist addition by phone before the timelock even starts.
3.lesson: A direct payment will always bounce. Get added to the allowlist first, wait out the delay, then get paid.
